name: Reference links
author: Brett
description: Text in the banners (In progress, Ready to merge, Merged, Live, the build and status banners, Codebase changes) that mentions a real part of the app is a link: a screen, a settings tab, section or single setting, a plugin, dialog, toolbar, menu, component, build, PR, agent or file. Tap = a peek card (what it is, where it lives, whether a build is changing it), double-tap = open it and highlight it, hold or right-click = Open, Open in new window, Show in UI Review, Show the build that's changing it, Copy link. A build's declared refs ('touches: settings.terminal, toolbar.terminal') win over names. Plain matching from the console's own registries (ref@1), no model, no tokens. Also over REST, the MCP tools ref_links_find / ref_links_resolve / ref_links_open and `axf ref-links …`.

items.title: Every reference target
items.description: Every thing a reference can point at right now: builds (with what they declare they touch, PR, UI Review items), plugins, the open console's screens, dialogs and settings tabs, agents.

items.title: Find references in text
items.description: The mentions of real things in a line of text (screens, settings, plugins, toolbars, builds, PRs, files…), each with the ref id it points at. Explicit touches win over names.

text.description: the text (a banner entry, a build title, a note)

touches.description: explicit refs that win, e.g. settings.terminal, toolbar.terminal

items.output: ref@1 { spans: [{ start, end, text, ref, kind, via, ambiguous?, candidates?, missing? }], refs, targets }

items.title: Resolve one reference
items.description: One ref by id (settings.terminal, screen:plan-studio, build:<id>, #123) or by a few words ("terminal settings").

items.title: Open what a reference points at
items.description: Brett's open console opens it and highlights it (like double-tapping the link): how = open (default), window (a new window), review (its UI Review item) or build (the build changing it). Only navigates.

to.description: recent (default), all, or a console client id

items.output: the console's answer (delivered: what each open console did)
